ecu_aps.label: Throttle
ecu_aps.note: Range [0, 110] %: the pedal channel reads 104-106 % at full throttle on every development session (pedal / ECU calibration over-range, not a fault). A [0, 100] gate failed the channel on 7 of 14 sessions (in-range share 0.36-0.47 < channel_quality_gates.failed_below) and left every entry_1_brake phase empty. 110 covers the observed maximum (106.0) with margin.

log_dms_dam_fl.label: Damper Force FL
log_dms_dam_fl.note: Damper/pushrod strain-gauge force sensor (modules/wheel_loads.py). Range gate = plausibility bound on pushrod force for this car (a few kN, generous both ways), not a sensor spec: admits real dynamic excursions, fails a grossly corrupted channel (see log_dms_dam_fr).

log_dms_dam_fr.label: Damper Force FR
log_dms_dam_fr.note: Same channel family as log_dms_dam_fl. On GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt the raw channel carries a constant corrupted offset (~-15.95 million N), removed by channel_corrections.log_dms_dam_fr before this gate. Uncorrected, the gate fails the channel (channel_quality_gates.failed_below) and wheel_loads falls back per corner instead of consuming the fault value.

ecu_B_tc_act.label: TC Active
ecu_B_tc_act.note: Traction-control activity flag (clean boolean; fired on only 3 samples in GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt, a session-data limitation, not a channel-quality one). Read by modules/setup_engine.py (tc_activity): a traction-limited exit ranks tc_lon above the differential. TC position: a position pair exists in all 14 development files in three agreeing domains (ecu_TC_int_pos / ecu_TC_tim_pos, log_tc_int_pos / log_tc_tim_pos, stw_rt03_tc_int / stw_rt01_tc_tim), but the LAT / LON mapping is undocumented and cannot be inferred (the values run nearly parallel), so no position channel is whitelisted and TC stays 'current value not assessable' (author ruling).

log_abs_pos.label: ABS Map Position (logged)
log_abs_pos.note: Trusted ABS switch-position channel (author decision). On GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt log_abs_pos / log_rt_abs_pos / stw_rt04_abs (dash / steering-wheel domain) agree at a constant 5; the ECU-domain abs_switch_pos reads 6 and is not trusted. Range [0, 11] = the rows of car_data.json's abs table (0 = off .. 11 = monsoon emergency). modules/setup_state.py reads the current ABS map from it, since the setup sheet has no ABS field.

log_susp_travel_fl.label: Suspension Travel FL
log_susp_travel_fl.note: Wheel/suspension travel (modules/wheel_loads.py) -- used to look up car_data.json motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel. Range is a generous mechanical-travel bound (car_data.json's own digitised table spans roughly -80..+60mm across both axles), not a precision spec.

corner_detection.brake_throttle_max_pct_derived_from: Tier B, value predates the records. The lift-off construction at 95 (last sample at or above it before turn-in = end of full throttle) was verified on 2026-08-20 against brake pressure on Dubai, 56 corner instances: brake-pressure rise after the lift-off point median 0.135 s front / 0.130 s rear, 0 % negative, n 36 (thesis_notes 'entry_1_brake phase-boundary bug'). The construction is verified; the value 95 itself is not derived (author ruling 2026-10-21).
corner_detection.steering_unwind_fraction_derived_from: Tier B, no derivation: exit_4 ends where the post-apex steering has unwound to half its post-apex peak -- the midpoint of the unwinding. Declared 2026-10-21 (author ruling), listed as a limitation in PRODUCTION.md 12.
corner_detection.lap_time_representative_factor_derived_f: 2026-09-03, corner canonicalisation fix. Representative laps cluster within ~1% of the session's fastest valid lap on both real sessions checked (Dubai worst ratio 1.0044, v3 worst representative ratio 1.0097, lap 6); the one excluded outlier observed (v3 lap 9, an on-track incident) sits at ratio 1.097141. SWEPT and confirmed, not just argued: v3's corner count is exactly 17 for every tested factor in (1.0097, 1.097141) -- the transition happens precisely between 1.0971 (17 corners, lap 9 still excluded) and 1.0972 (20 corners, lap 9 now included) -- so the result is not just 'roughly insensitive', it is provably constant on that entire open interval by construction (the filter depends only on the derived representative-lap SET, which is a step function of the factor with steps exactly at each lap's own ratio). Re-examine this factor if a session produces a genuinely intermediate lap (e.g. a traffic-compromised lap around ratio 1.04) -- that case is unobserved in the data checked so far.

channel_corrections._comment: Decoding offsets for known-corrupt channels, applied in csv_parser before the quality/range gate, only if the file's raw channel mean lies inside precondition_mean_range (a healthy export stays untouched). Three offset classes: decoding faults (this block, e.g. v3 FR), event-specific logger zero entries (event_zero_entries, applied right after this block) and the static gauge-check calibration (wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, after the gate).

log_dms_dam_fr.derived_from: GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt gauge forensics (2026-09-04) found log_dms_dam_fr carries real, correctly-signed pushrod-force signal (whole-session std=1864.2N, matching the three healthy corners' own 1925.9/2082.5/2007.3N) riding on a stationary corrupted additive offset (whole-session raw mean -15949976.44N) -- pure rescaling (x1e-3/x1e-6) was ruled out since the raw fluctuation is ALREADY at the correct physical scale. 2026-09-18: the offset was anchored empirically once a real per-outing weighing existed: K is chosen so FR's own straight-line raw mean, scaled by the tiny FR/FL static-weight ratio from the outing's real corner weighing (298.9/300.3 kg), matches FL's own straight-line raw mean -- FR is FL's own axle mate, sharing the same motion-ratio table and (per that weighing) nearly equal static load. VALIDATED against the full wheel_loads.py decomposition chain (diagnostics/inspect_deepening_phase2_fr_correction.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22)): straight-line total load +10.77% vs session weight (matches the already-recorded, aero-explained +11.64% v3 finding from when FR was on static fallback); corr(ay,Fz_fr)=+0.893, corr(ay,Fz_fl)=-0.903 (both strong, correctly signed, close to this project's own healthy-corner reference band +0.966/-0.893 to -0.895); FR/FL straight-line static means within 2-3% of the outing's own real corner weights on BOTH corners equally (a shared aero-lift bias, not an FR-specific error) -- FL/FR ratio 0.9970 vs the weighing's own 1.0047 (0.77% apart). One clean pass, no red flags -- FR promoted from the axle-total reconstruction fallback to a live, damper-measured Level 4 corner on this file.

event_zero_entries._comment: Event-specific logger zero entries (author ruling). A gauge zeroed against a different reference at one event reads a constant offset there; csv_parser subtracts zero_N from the raw channel BEFORE the quality/range gate (the gate otherwise fails the channel and wheel_loads drops to the static split). An entry applies to a file only if (a) the header's TrackName and logger serial (SystemDetails 'Serial Number') match, and (b) GATE-WINDOW GUARD: the channel's raw mean minus zero_N lies inside that channel's own range gate in 'channels' -- no new tunable; a gauge re-zeroed at a later event of the same track fails the guard and stays on the static split instead of silently taking a wrong entry. Accuracy: wheel loads from a corrected channel are 'L4 with an L2 zero' (L4-rel): logged sensor + motion-ratio table (L4), zero entry an event measurement pinned through the same car's Paul Ricard zero (L2, per-corner u below).
event_zero_entries._procedure: How an event gets its entry (documented, not automated): (1) census the event's files -- header track / serial, raw damper level vs the range gate; (2) preferred: the team's static zero check at the event, entered as a measured zero; otherwise the recovery rule of inspect_recover_rr.py (git tag pre-prune-2026-10-22) -- per file and corner, the gauge-vs-raw-voltage map offset (Input 21 / 29 / 31 / 39 Voltage -> FL / FR / RL / RR, inventory maps of inspect_v4_windows.py, same tag) minus the same car's Paul Ricard map offset, median over the event's files; (3) acceptance: u <= 700 N wheel and V1-V4 on all files of the event; (4) enter the medians with file spread and u. inspect_recover_rr.py is hard-wired to the 16 NBR files, so step (2) needs that script generalised for a new event. LIMITATION (author ruling): the header carries no date, so two events of the same track and logger whose zeros are near-identical (both passing the guard) cannot be told apart -- recorded, not solved.

NBR_221.derived_from: Q-RECOVER-2 R3, 2026-10-03 (diagnostics/inspect_recover_rr.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), author-ruled reference, recover.json): the NBR event's damper gauges were zeroed against a different reference than every other event of this car (zero entry about +43 kN vs about -15.5 kN). zero_N per corner = median over the 16 NBR files of (NBR gauge-vs-voltage map offset - the same car's Paul Ricard map offset), the Paul Ricard reference = mean of v3 and pr_us_v2; u_wheel_N = sqrt((MR x sqrt(SD^2 + e_PR^2))^2 + 98^2), dominated by the Paul Ricard zero residual e_PR. V1-V4 pass on all 16 files (Q-RECOVER-2). Config corner weights are a guideline (rule 0). FR COUPLING: the FR entry was referenced to the Paul Ricard FR map offset INCLUDING the channel_corrections log_dms_dam_fr value (+15,954,360 N); if that correction is ever re-derived, this FR entry must be re-derived with it (the two never act on the same file -- the correction's mean-range precondition cannot match NBR).

PRC_221_24996.derived_from: 2026-10-27, review ruling (evaluation package; no per-session tare, event entry as NBR_221). diagnostics/inspect_prc24996_zero.py, diagnostics/output/prc24996_zero.json. The Paul Ricard exports with logger software (Metafile) 24996 read the damper gauges about 5 kN (gauge) low at standstill, sign and scale correct (corr with outside a_y +0.83..+0.87, moving std as on the healthy files); the 25016 exports of the same car and track read correctly. Track + serial alone cannot separate them (gate-window guard passes both), hence the logger_software key. zero_N per corner = median over the source sessions (PRC outing 41 session 3, PRC outing 43 session 3) of [median damper force over standstill-on-wheels samples (v < 1 km/h, travel within +-5 mm of the session's pit-lane rolling median on all four corners, >= 1.0 s) - static corner load W g / MR (setup-sheet corner weights, MR at standstill travel)]. u_gauge_N = sqrt(e_between^2 + e_ref^2), e_between = half the source spread, e_ref = RMS of the same method's offsets on the healthy Paul Ricard files PRC outings 27, 32, 33 and LC 25 (they need no zero, so their offset is the method's own error, mostly the corner-weight guideline: -1.0..+0.04 kN gauge); u_wheel_N = u_gauge_N x MR at standstill. Source residuals +-65..182 N gauge. validation_envelope = min-max of wheel_loads.load_validation_quantities on the same four healthy files (offset-free checks, parameters.json wheel_loads.zero_validation); a session from source_sessions has its zero from its own standstill, so the static-weight plausibility check is reported as not applicable there and these checks carry the validation. Accuracy: wheel loads L4 with an L2 zero, as NBR_221.
